rounds.fact: Answers.com built its early traffic by aggregating dictionary, encyclopedia, and reference content into a single searchable site, well before crowdsourced Q&A sites took over that space.
Netscape's browser dominated the early web so completely that Microsoft bundling Internet Explorer with Windows to compete became the center of a landmark antitrust case.
Plenty of Fish was famously built and run by a single person for years, supported entirely by ads, before eventually being sold for hundreds of millions of dollars.
Tumblr popularized the short-form 'microblogging' format, and grew so fast in its early years that it regularly had to fight off downtime from its own success.
Snopes started in 1994 as a husband-and-wife hobby project cataloging urban legends, long before 'fact-checking' became a major, sometimes controversial, category of website.
